concept: Perpetual futures and margin on Solana: Drift/Velocity, Jupiter Perps, Zeta, Flash, with Hyperliquid and CEX comparison
summary: Perpetual-futures margin and liquidation on Solana venues (Drift and its successor Velocity, Jupiter Perps, Zeta, Flash Trade) compared with Hyperliquid and Binance, from 590 research units; cross margin pools collateral across positions while isolated margin confines it to one position (Hyperliquid docs; Drift and Velocity apply cross margin per subaccount). Evidence status: research claims ungated (v4 evidence gate not passed); treat as leads with cited sources. Educational reading aid, not financial advice; leverage can lose more than the stake.

facts.text: On Drift, the cross-margin scope is the subaccount. Inside one subaccount, every deposit and every position is cross-margined, and health is computed over the whole account. Between subaccounts nothing is shared, and a liquidation in one leaves the others untouched. Neodyme's 2024 audit says margin calculations are isolated between a customer's User accounts. Each subaccount has hard limits of 8 perp positions, 8 spot positions and 32 orders.

Hyperliquid's docs say cross margin is the default and isolated margin is also supported, which constrains an asset's collateral to that asset. A liquidation of an isolated position does not affect cross positions, and a cross liquidation does not affect isolated positions.

Bullet describes itself as a 'network extension': a dedicated execution layer for perps, spot and lending that posts transactions back to Solana. Its FAQ says Solana provides consensus, data availability and settlement and claims about 2 ms latency; Solana Compass describes a Rust matching engine with FIFO sequencing and claims sub-1 ms soft confirmation and 30,000 orders per second at launch. Bullet's docs index lists sequencer, orderbook, unified margin engine, liquidation and insurance fund/ADL pages. All performance figures are vendor claims.

Each collateral spot market has its own Insurance Fund, held in that market's own asset. Spot bad debt draws on that asset's fund. Every perp is quoted and settled in the quote asset, so all perp bad debt draws on the quote market's fund. Neodyme described this design for Drift v2 in its May and June 2024 audit, and Velocity's docs describe the same structure.

On Drift and Velocity, cross margin applies inside one subaccount only. Every deposit in a subaccount backs every position in it. A deposit in one subaccount does not back a position in another, and subaccount 0 neither backs nor endangers subaccount 1. Neodyme's 2024 audit says margin calculations are isolated between a customer's User accounts. Velocity's program-structure page calls each subaccount its own margin silo.

As of 2026-11-06, Velocity's docs describe cross margin inside each subaccount and no per-position isolated margin. Its docs index lists margin, account health, isolated pools and contract tiers pages, but no isolated-positions page. The program-structure page says each subaccount is its own margin silo. The release notes of the repository that Velocity forked from list isolated positions, so the docs and the code differ.

Hyperliquid liquidation sequence (its docs): liquidation starts when account equity falls below maintenance margin, defined as half of the initial margin at max leverage (1.25% of notional for 40x assets up to 16.7% for 3x assets). The engine first sends market orders for the full position to the order book; if that fully or partly closes the position and the maintenance requirement is met, the remaining collateral stays with the trader. Jupiter Perps' JLP-pool markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) charge no funding rate. They execute at oracle prices against the JLP pool. They charge a continuous, non-compounding borrow fee on the full position size: hourly rate = annual rate from a per-custody jump-rate utilization curve / 8,760, taken from collateral when the position changes. The beta-markets page confirms that these markets pay a borrow fee, not funding, and that their liquidation trigger is the oracle price.

Jupiter Perps' JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) have no funding rate and no separate mark price. They charge a non-compounding borrow fee on full position size: hourly rate = annual rate from a per-custody jump-rate utilization curve / 8,760, with longs using the traded asset's utilization and shorts the USDC custody's. The liquidation trigger is the oracle price, whereas the beta markets use a mark price.

On Jupiter Perps JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC), liquidation triggers when the oracle price crosses the liquidation price and the protocol takes all remaining collateral as the liquidation fee, so the trader gets nothing back. On Beta markets remaining collateral after loss and fees is returned to the trader. The Beta markets run on a separate engine that does not feed the JLP pool. The JLP pool is the counterparty, so trader profits are paid from the pool.

Hyperliquid's mark price is the median of three inputs: (1) oracle price plus a 150-second EMA of the gap between Hyperliquid's mid and the oracle; (2) the median of Hyperliquid's best bid, best ask and last trade; (3) the median of perp mid prices from Binance, OKX, Bybit, Gate IO and MEXC. The oracle is a weighted median of CEX spot prices updated by validators about every 3 seconds (CEX weights Binance 3, OKX 2, Bybit 2, Gate IO 1, MEXC 1). Mark is used for margining, liquidation, TP/SL triggers and unrealized PnL.

Hyperliquid's mark price is the median of three inputs: (1) the oracle price plus a 150-second EMA of (Hyperliquid mid - oracle); (2) the median of Hyperliquid's best bid, best ask and last trade; (3) the median of Binance, OKX, Bybit, Gate IO and MEXC perp mid prices with weights 3, 2, 2, 1, 1. If exactly two of the three inputs exist, a 30-second EMA of input (2) is added. Mark price drives margining, liquidations, TP/SL triggers and unrealized PnL. The oracle price, a weighted median of CEX spot prices that validators update about every 3 seconds, drives funding. The mark-price page is mark

After JELLY, the community-docs incident page lists Hyperliquid follow-ups: margin tiers launched 2025-05-22 (max leverage falls with position size), a cap on the liquidator vault relative to total HLP balance, ADL changes triggered when liquidator losses exceed a threshold, and on-chain delisting votes with open-interest caps scaled to market cap. The page is a community analysis, not an official Hyperliquid postmortem.

Hyperliquid builds its funding oracle and its mark price separately. Oracle: each validator publishes, about every 3 seconds, a weighted median of eight spot mids (Binance 3, OKX 2, Bybit 2, Kraken, Kucoin, Gate IO, MEXC and Hyperliquid 1 each), and the clearinghouse takes the stake-weighted median across validators. Mark: the median of (a) oracle plus a 150-second EMA of Hyperliquid mid minus oracle, (b) the median of Hyperliquid best bid, best ask and last trade, and (c) a weighted median of Binance, OKX, Bybit, Gate IO and MEXC perp mids (weights 3, 2, 2, 1, 1); if exactly two of the three

Hyperliquid says a cross position's actual liquidation price does not depend on its leverage setting, because lower leverage only locks more collateral. An isolated position's liquidation price does depend on leverage, because the isolated margin allocated equals the initial margin set. Funding payments and unrealized PnL on other cross positions can still move a cross liquidation price after the position opens.

Hyperliquid liquidation price formula (docs): liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side), where l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE, side = 1 for long and -1 for short, margin_available (cross) = account_value - maintenance_margin_required, and margin_available (isolated) = isolated_margin - maintenance_margin_required. For tiered assets, maintenance leverage comes from the margin tier matching position value at the liquidation price. The cross-margin liquidation price does not depend on the leverage setting; the isolated one does. Displayed estimates can drift with

Velocity's bad-debt waterfall for a perp market runs in this order: the liquidated account's estate (remaining deposit and P&L-pool claims), the market's in-transit insurance fee, the insurance fund up to the market's tier cap, the AMM fee-provision clawback, then socialization. Socialization spreads the residual across surviving open interest in that perp market through both cumulative funding rates. Spot shortfalls instead cut the deposit-interest index across depositors. Winning positions are not exempt.

Jupiter Perps' JLP-pool markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) charge no funding rate. They charge a continuous, non-compounding borrow fee on full position size: hourly rate = annual rate from a per-custody jump-rate utilization curve / 8,760, settled from collateral when the position changes. Longs use the market asset's utilization; shorts use the USDC custody's utilization.

Isolated margin limits a loss to the position's own collateral, but it can take all of that collateral. Solflare says isolated margin limits but does not eliminate loss, because a liquidation can take the position's full collateral. Jupiter's JLP markets take all remaining collateral as a liquidation fee. Hyperliquid does not return maintenance margin in a backstop liquidation. Flash Trade does not return remaining maintenance margin either. A trader who wants to keep part of the margin has to exit or place a stop before the liquidation price.

Drift and Velocity charge funding in quote units per unit of base asset. The stored rate is the clamped price spread divided by 24, and settlement multiplies the change in the cumulative rate by the position's base amount; no current price is applied at settlement. Hyperliquid and Zeta instead multiply a percentage rate by the oracle price and the position size.

Each Velocity action accepts a different set of grades. Auction-skipping AMM fills need Valid. Margin calculation and DLOB order matching reject non-positive, too volatile, too uncertain and stale-for-margin. Liquidation and trigger orders reject only non-positive and too volatile. TWAP and AMM-curve updates reject only non-positive. Funding updates and P&L settlement accept Valid, stale-for-AMM, insufficient data points and stale-for-margin. A code comment cites audit finding OtterSec #142 as the reason order matching uses the margin rule.

Hyperliquid's backstop liquidation reaches only the margin pool of the failing mode. It applies when equity falls below 2/3 of maintenance margin and order-book liquidation has not restored the account. A cross backstop liquidation transfers all the trader's cross positions and cross margin to the liquidator vault, which leaves zero equity if the trader has no isolated positions. An isolated backstop liquidation transfers only that position and its isolated margin, and leaves cross margin and positions untouched.

On Hyperliquid, the margin mode sets how much a backstop liquidation takes. Backstop liquidation applies when equity falls below two thirds of maintenance margin and order-book liquidation has not restored the account. A cross backstop liquidation transfers all of the trader's cross positions and cross margin to the liquidator vault, which leaves zero equity if the trader holds no isolated position. An isolated backstop liquidation transfers only that position and its isolated margin. The maintenance margin is not returned to the trader in either case.

Isolation does not shield a trader's counterparties. Hyperliquid's auto-deleveraging rule covers isolated positions: when a user's account value or an isolated position value turns negative, traders on the opposite side are ranked by unrealized PnL and leverage, and their positions close at the previous mark price against the underwater user. OtterSec's reverse engineering reports that strict-isolated assets skip the aggregate-shortfall gate and go straight into the ADL queue. That finding rests on testnet state, and the author says mainnet metadata is hard to verify.

Bullet's docs describe a USDC insurance fund that covers a shortfall when liquidation fails, then ADL as the last line: traders are ranked by leverage and unrealized P&L, and profitable high-leverage positions are reduced. The docs claim this avoids socialized loss. A banner says Bullet is replacing ADL with 'social deleverage (SDL)' and an updated page is coming. A backstop liquidator vault takes over failing positions at the bankruptcy price. The pages carry no date.

A Hyperliquid community wiki (pro-Hyperliquid, unofficial) lists post-JELLY changes: the liquidator vault capped to a small share of HLP with isolated collateral, ADL triggered when liquidator losses exceed a threshold, onchain delisting by validator vote, open-interest caps scaled to market capitalization, and margin tiers launched 2025-05-22. These items were not found in the official docs pages fetched on 2026-11-06.

Hyperliquid backstop liquidation differs by mode. In cross mode, all cross positions and cross margin transfer to the liquidator. In isolated mode, only that isolated position and its isolated margin transfer, and the user's cross margin and positions are untouched. The trigger is account equity below 2/3 of maintenance margin after the order-book attempt fails.

Hyperliquid portfolio margin extends cross margin to margin eligible spot assets (HYPE, BTC, USDC, USDT) and perp positions together, with automatic borrowing against collateral at set LTVs (HYPE 0.65 and BTC 0.5 on the page). An account becomes liquidatable when portfolio_margin_ratio > 0.95. Eligibility needs a master account with more than $5M weighted volume or more than $10k account value, and account value under $25M.

Hyperliquid portfolio margin generalizes cross margin. It margins all cross-margin perp positions and eligible spot balances together in one account, and sub-accounts stay separate. The account becomes liquidatable when portfolio_margin_ratio exceeds 0.95. Eligible collateral can be borrowed against at a set LTV: the page gives HYPE 0.65 and BTC 0.5. The page says accounts fall back to non-portfolio behavior when supply or borrow caps are hit. The account abstraction page lists HYPE, BTC, USDC and USDT as the eligible assets.

A Velocity spot bankruptcy draws first on the bad-debt market's own revenue pool, which is first-loss capital. It then draws on that market's Insurance Fund vault, always leaving at least one token. Last, it cuts the deposit-interest index for every lender in that market, never below 1. Perp bankruptcies must resolve before spot ones, because both draw on the same quote vault. A spot resolution fails with PerpBankruptcyMustPrecedeSpot while a cross-margin perp bankruptcy is unresolved.

Hyperliquid's docs say a cross position's liquidation price does not depend on the leverage setting, because lower leverage only locks more collateral. An isolated position's liquidation price does depend on leverage, because the isolated margin allocated equals the initial margin set. The documented formula is liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side), with l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE and side = 1 for longs and -1 for shorts. margin_available is account_value - maintenance_margin_required for cross and isolated_margin - maintenance_margin_required for isola

Velocity's perp bankruptcy order is: step 0, the estate pays first (its perp P&L-pool claims, then its own quote deposit); tranche 1, the market's in-transit insurance fee; tranche 2, the shared quote insurance fund vault, limited by the market's remaining tier claim and by the vault balance minus 1 token; tranche 3, a clawback of the fee provision granted to the AMM; then socialization across surviving open interest. The velocity-v1 resolve_perp_bankruptcy code and the docs agree on this order.

The Insurance Fund also pays through a second path that is not a bankruptcy: resolve_perp_pnl_deficit. It moves quote tokens from the fund into a perp market's P&L pool only when the AMM is underwater (total_fee_minus_distributions below zero), the P&L pool is smaller than net user P&L, and net unsettled P&L exceeds the market's unrealized_pnl_max_imbalance. The draw is the smallest of the excess imbalance, the remaining per-period withdrawal allowance, the remaining lifetime insurance cap, and the vault balance minus one token. Velocity's docs say this draw covers a P&L deficit, not funding,

A stale feed degrades Velocity in steps. The AMM stops quoting first, while orderbook matching, margin and liquidation continue. Once the feed is stale for margin, margin-gated actions revert, including opening a position and withdrawing collateral while holding liabilities, even on markets the account does not trade. Liquidations and trigger orders still run, so a stale price does not protect an underwater account.

A non-peer-reviewed preprint on the 2025-10-10 cascade reports that Binance priced USDe collateral from its own order book, so USDe fell to $0.65 there while staying near par elsewhere, and that Hyperliquid's multi-exchange weighted-median oracle did not follow. The author states the mechanism is not identified causally, the cascade regime rests on about 353 observations, and the study covers only BTC on two venues. The episode concerned collateral pricing, not perp mark price.

Velocity bankruptcy resolution is permissionless: anyone may resolve a latched perp or spot bankruptcy. A solvency flag, separate from the general withdraw pauses and flippable only by the cold-admin key, gates it. An admin can therefore pause withdrawals without blocking bad-debt resolution. Only the Velocity docs state this; the instruction code was not checked for the flag.

The Drift program stores isolated collateral on the perp position itself. PerpPosition.isolated_position_scaled_balance holds a quote-asset deposit, and PositionFlag::IsolatedPosition marks the position. MarginCalculation keeps one IsolatedMarginCalculation per perp market index beside the single cross calculation. An isolated position's collateral is its deposit value plus weighted PnL, and its requirement is separate from the cross requirement. meets_margin_requirement() returns true only if the cross calculation and every isolated calculation pass. Drift's insurance fund also tops up a perp market's P&L pool, which is not a bankruptcy. resolve_perp_pnl_deficit pays only when the AMM's total fee minus distributions is negative, the P&L pool holds less than users' net P&L, and net unsettled P&L exceeds the market's configured unrealized_pnl_max_imbalance. The payment is the smallest of that excess, the market's remaining per-period revenue-withdraw allowance, its remaining tier claim, and the vault balance minus 1 token. Neodyme describes the same instruction.

Integrators can pre-check Drift's oracle grading client-side with the SDK in src/math/oracles.ts: getOracleValidity(market, oraclePriceData, oracleGuardRails, slot, oracleStalenessBuffer = 5) returns the grade, isOracleValid gives the AMM-only check, isOracleTooDivergent tests the 5-minute TWAP band, and oraclePriceBands derives a band from the initial-minus-maintenance margin ratio gap. The file mirrors, and does not replace, the on-chain program.

Drift's oracle TWAP uses the exchange oracle price, clamped by the same tier bands as mark samples, over two windows (the funding period and 5 minutes). If the oracle was invalid for a stretch, the next oracle-TWAP update is interpolated toward the mark TWAP in proportion to the outage. An admin instruction, `ResetPerpMarketAmmOracleTwap`, can reset the oracle TWAP to the mark TWAP when it is badly out of balance (Neodyme).

Jupiter Perps charges a flat 0.06% base fee on trade size when opening and when closing. Borrow fees accrue hourly with no compounding, from a per-asset utilization curve. A price impact fee has a linear part (at least 0.01%; SOL adds 0.01% per roughly $375,000 of size) and an additive part that applies only when a trade worsens a long/short imbalance above a threshold. Base, linear and additive fees together are capped at 0.50%.

trade.xyz defines the mark price of its HIP-3 perps as the median of (1) the oracle price, (2) the oracle price plus a 150-second EMA of (perp mid - oracle), and (3) the median of best bid, best ask and last trade. It has no cross-exchange perp-mid input. The relayer's updates to oracle and mark are clamped to +/-50 bps of the current value. While the external market is closed, the oracle advances by an EMA (30-minute time constant) of the book's own impact price difference, so the funding reference is then partly endogenous.

Flash Trade's docs say its margining engine 'does not require an insurance fund' because the pool backing each position is always the counterparty. Keeper bots liquidate once a position crosses maintenance, and any remaining maintenance margin goes to liquidity providers, not back to the trader. Maintenance leverage is a per-pool parameter, as of 2026-07-03. Flash announced a wind-down on 2026-08-07.

A Drift/Velocity market with no listed feed can use a prelaunch oracle that is self-referential: its price is the market's own mark TWAP, capped at an admin-set max_price, and its confidence is the larger of the ask/bid TWAP spread and the mark standard deviation (PrelaunchOracle::update). Velocity says such markets sit in the tiers with no insurance coverage and the widest confidence tolerance because they have no outside anchor.

Drift's 1 April 2026 exploit drained about $295M (Drift's own figure: $295,426,725.97), with JLP the largest stolen asset at about $159.3M. Drift states the Insurance Fund was unaffected because the protocol paused before liquidation or bankruptcy losses were completed. All Insurance Fund depositors' assets were made available for withdrawal on 7 July 2026.

None of the Jupiter pages read describes an insurance fund, a bad-debt waterfall or ADL for the JLP markets. The liquidation page, Perps overview, Perps FAQ, JLP earn page, April 2026 JLP assessment and an independent analysis all leave bad debt unaddressed. This is an absence in public documentation. It does not prove the program has no backstop.

Hyperliquid evaluates an 8-hour funding formula but pays every hour at one eighth of the computed rate. It samples the premium every 5 seconds and averages it over the hour. The payment is position_size x oracle_price x funding_rate. The oracle price, not the mark price, converts size to notional. The trade.xyz HIP-3 docs restate the hourly one-eighth rule and the oracle-price notional.

Neodyme's May 2024 audit of Drift v2 found a Critical bug (ND-DFT1-CR-01, resolved) that used the bankruptcy path to extract value. A flat $0.01 keeper reward could be triggered twice per order, so an attacker-controlled maker could be driven into debt without a margin check. ResolveSpotBankruptcy then socialized the debt or drew the insurance fund while the filler kept the fees. Neodyme estimated about $250k per day.

Insurance funds can be drained by engineered bankruptcies. Neodyme's audit finding ND-DFT1-CR-01 (Critical, resolved) showed that a flat $0.01 keeper fee, charged without a margin check, could be triggered twice per order. An attacker could push a controlled maker account into debt, then call ResolveSpotBankruptcy to socialize the loss or cover it from the Insurance Fund, and repeat the cycle. Neodyme estimated a drain of about $250k per day. The same audit says a keeper that updates the perp bid/ask TWAP must have at least $1,000 staked in the Insurance Fund.

For derivatives and perps, Pyth's docs recommend delayed settlement (round the trade timestamp up to the next channel interval so the trader could not have seen the price), spread pricing using the lower/upper confidence bound, minimum hold times, no same-block open/close, caps on per-trade notional, per-block volume and per-market open interest, wider spreads or size caps under stress, and pausing new positions if updates stall.
Jupiter's Beta markets (stock perps) skip the keeper and custody-account model. Orders go to a separate orderbook engine called GUM, and the stock prices come from Chainlink oracles.

Flash Trade's docs do not name a margin mode. They describe collateral position by position: shorts always post USDC, and each long market has a fixed backing asset in its pool (SOL longs use JitoSOL, BNB and XRP longs use BTC, equities use SPY). The user can pay with another balance, and the protocol swaps it into the backing asset for a pool swap fee. Flash says it needs no insurance fund because the pool is always the counterparty.

In the archived Drift v2 code, stored Lazer confidence is the best-ask minus best-bid spread, or price/500 (20 bp) when bid is not below ask or a side is missing. Velocity stores the widest of three: price/LAZER_CONF_FLOOR_DIVISOR (500), the bid-ask spread, and the message's signed Confidence property. The code comment says the stored value never understates what the message reports. So Lazer-market 'confidence' is not the publisher-dispersion interval that Pyth Core documents.

On Velocity, update_funding_rate runs only when the market's funding period has elapsed on the hour grid. If the previous update landed more than one third of a period (20 minutes for a one-hour period) after the hour, the next update waits until the following period. The program skips the update if funding is paused, the oracle is invalid, or the mark and oracle prices diverge too far. Funding accrues into per-market cumulative long and short rates. Zeta's docs define funding over 24 hours as impactMidpoint / oracle - 1, where the impact midpoint is the order-book midpoint at $1,000 of quotes on each side. Payment = funding rate x oracle x position size, and longs pay when the rate is positive. Zeta recalculates about every 10 seconds and applies funding on balance-sensitive operations (placeOrder, withdraw, liquidate) and through cranks about every couple of minutes. The page is marked 'Last updated 2 years ago', so the parameters may be stale.

Bullet's own docs describe restricted access. Its FAQ (marked 'Last updated 3 months ago' when fetched on 2026-11-06) says 'Bullet is currently on gated mainnet' and requires an invite code; its ZEX Booster page calls Bullet an 'invite-only private beta, with a limited number of traders onboarded so far' and says Bullet Points have not launched. Its docs index marks the zero-knowledge virtual machine and Data Availability architecture pages 'In development'. Solana Compass instead says Bullet mainnet launched publicly on 2025-09-29 with SP1 zero-knowledge proofs and Celestia data availability,

Hyperliquid's 'no bad debt' property is produced by ADL, not by an absence of shortfalls. The ADL docs say ADL strictly keeps the platform solvent so it has no bad debt. Chitra's v3 reconstruction of Oct 10, 2025 estimates an aggregate loser-side deficit of about $100.1M that winners' profits covered; CoinGecko summarizes the same day as record liquidations 'without incurring any bad debt'. Read 'no bad debt' as 'losses were socialized to winners', which is the cost CEX traders also bear when a Binance insurance fund is exhausted.

Chitra's paper (arXiv 2512.01112) calls ADL a last-resort loss-socialization mechanism and proves a trilemma: no ADL policy can satisfy exchange solvency, exchange revenue and trader fairness together. It treats the insurance fund as the first line of defense and ADL as the way to socialize what remains. It argues queue policies, such as Binance's and Hyperliquid's, can concentrate losses on top winners, and it names pro-rata, which it attributes to Drift and Paradex, the fairness benchmark.

Zeta's docs (undated, possibly legacy) say Pyth is the primary oracle with per-slot updates and is used without consulting the secondary whenever its price is valid and recent enough. Chainlink is the secondary and is used when Pyth is too stale. If both are stale, Zeta averages the last prices of both, and uses the average only if it is recent and stable. The page does not mention Switchboard, mark-price use or confidence handling. Single-source reading of the page via a summarizing fetch; the saved text snapshot kept only navigation.

Pyth's own best-practices page leaves integrators to enforce limits: on-chain verifyUpdate checks signature and fee but not update age; confidence thresholds have no recommended value. When confidence is wide it suggests using the EMA price or pausing new activity that depends on the price. A Pyth blog post says leveraged markets could reduce available margin on a low-confidence price and be more conservative with liquidations.

The Velocity program source is public. The GitHub repository velocity-exchange/velocity-v1 is public under Apache-2.0, holds the on-chain programs (velocity, vaults, jit-proxy), SDKs and a Drift-to-Velocity migration guide, and took a merge on 2026-11-04. Solana Compass reports the code was published on 2026-09-17. The Velocity docs home page still says the program 'is not open source yet', so that sentence is out of date. The velocity-exchange organisation appears to be the renamed drift-labs organisation: it hosts the archived Drift protocol-v2 repository, and drift-labs/protocol-v2 redirect

Drift's on-chain program distinguishes three margin requirement types: Initial, Fill and Maintenance. Fill is the average of the market's initial and maintenance margin ratios. Drift's docs likewise say fill checks use the midpoint of the scaled initial and maintenance weights.

FTI Consulting says unified (cross-asset) margin is efficient in calm markets but ties portfolios to their weakest assets under stress, because long-only collateral sell-offs may not be offset by short profits. It says venues that priced collateral from their own spot markets marked USDe down sharply during the 10 October 2025 crash and pushed thousands of accounts through maintenance thresholds. CoinShares reports USDe fell to $0.65 on Binance and that Binance priced these assets from internal spot markets, not external oracles.

Binance's USDS-M mark price is Median(Price 1, Price 2, Contract Price). Price 1 = price index x (1 + last funding rate x time until next funding / funding period). Price 2 = price index + a 30-second moving average of the per-second basis ((bid1 + ask1) / 2 - index); before 2025-09-18 08:01 UTC the window was 1 minute. Binance values funding payments at mark price (nominal value = mark price x contract size), whereas Hyperliquid values them at the oracle price.

In Drift's program, MarginCalculation keeps a separate IsolatedMarginCalculation per perp market index, each with its own margin_requirement and total_collateral. An account meets its margin requirement only if the cross calculation and every isolated calculation each pass, so isolated shortfalls are checked independently of cross collateral.

OtterSec's decompile of the Hyperliquid node found an undocumented conditional insurance mechanism. The clearinghouse runs its ADL check at the end of every block. If total shortfall is below a constant (hardcoded to $5M in the testnet state), cross-margin positions are spared from ADL. Markets flagged strict_isolated (on testnet including HYPE, ZRO and JELLYJELLY) skip that tolerance and go straight to the ADL queue. OtterSec says mainnet values are unverified. Sepper separately estimates Hyperliquid's pre-event insurance fund at about $25M 'from public data'.

Drift v1 (May 2022) is the platform's own example of an insurance fund draw. The protocol paused on 2022-05-11 during the LUNA crash, with a $10.11M withdrawable-collateral shortfall. The post-mortem names three causes: users could withdraw positive realized P&L before matching losses were realized; users could draw on the Insurance Fund with no limits, so one market's losses spilled across all markets; and leverage did not tighten as long-short imbalance grew. Drift sunset v1 and repaid $19.5M of settled collateral in full: $4.95M from the remaining Insurance Fund and $14.55M from financing.

Per the Gauntlet paper, BitMEX ranked ADL candidates by profit times leverage starting in 2016, Binance used the same formula from 2019, and Hyperliquid uses a queue derived from Huobi's 2015 design. The paper says queue-based methods are the worst policies for the top winning trade.

Pyth's best-practices page says on-chain verifyUpdate checks the signature and fee but not the update's age, so the integrator must enforce a freshness threshold. It warns that transaction submitters choose which signed update to include, which is functionally equivalent to seeing a future price, and that latency-sensitive protocols may cut the threshold to a few seconds. Velocity's Lazer instruction is a concrete implementation of such a bound.

Neither margin mode is strictly safer. Isolated margin confines a loss to one position's collateral but removes netting, so the position reaches liquidation sooner. Cross margin lets profits offset losses and delays liquidation, but it couples positions through shared collateral, so one bad position or one collateral mark-down can consume the whole account. FTI says unified margin ties portfolios to their weakest assets under stress. OneKey says cross margin is not automatically safer because it exposes the whole balance.

Both codebases let the AMM absorb long/short imbalance but cap what it pays. Legacy Drift limits AMM-paid funding to one third of the fee pool above a lower bound per funding period (the `safe_div(3)` rule is present in the file since 2022-10-28); Velocity limits it to one third of retained equity (`total_fee_minus_distributions`) and says the insurance fund is never used. When the cap binds, the receiving side's rate is cut so the AMM's outflow fits.

On Drift-lineage programs a Pyth Lazer price is posted by a permissionless keeper. The program checks the Lazer message signature through a signature-verify instruction against the Pyth Lazer storage account, then writes price, publish_time, posted_slot, exponent and conf to a per-feed PythLazerOracle account. It rejects a zero price as 'not enough publishers'.

Flash Trade's Pricing Engine page names Pyth as its primary pricing reference and says Flash uses a proprietary backup oracle system, with no detail on how it works or when it takes over. It prices its price-impact fee against Pyth Pro feeds at the instant of opening, to cover oracle-update landing latency.

For Pyth pull and Lazer accounts, Drift's Rust computes oracle delay as clock_slot minus the slot in which the update was posted (posted_slot) and keeps publish_time as a sequence id. Pyth's own guidance is that verifyUpdate checks the signature and fee but not the update's age, so each integrator must enforce freshness, and that transaction submitters choose which signed update to include.

Drift's funding update is permissionless and lazy. The `update_funding_rate` instruction has no signer in its account list and only applies when `on_the_hour_update` returns zero; an update that lands later than one third of the period (20 minutes) past the hour pushes the next update a full period later. Payments are credited separately: each account settles against per-side cumulative rates on its next action, and `SettleFundingPayment` is permissionless (Neodyme). When bad debt exceeded a Solana venue's designed backstops, the outcome came from governance. At Mango Markets (October 2022) one attacker account ended with about $115.2M of bad debt and another with $11.3M of uncollectible debt (CertiK), and the DAO voted to let the attacker keep $47M and return $67M (CertiK and Ackee). Academic work treats funding as the mechanism that substitutes for expiry convergence: because perpetuals never mature, longs pay shorts a rate tied to the perp-spot gap. He et al. derive no-arbitrage prices and find crypto perp deviations larger than in traditional FX, shrinking over time. Kim and Park propose path-dependent funding rates as a practical alternative.

Zeta defines funding as impactMidpoint / oracle - 1, where impactMidpoint is the orderbook midpoint given $1000 of quotes on each side; payment is fundingRate * oracle * positionSize, with positive rates paid by longs. Rates are calculated about every 10 seconds and applied during balance-sensitive operations (placeOrder, withdraw, liquidate) and by cranks about every couple of minutes. The docs state no funding cap.

Binance perpetual mark price is Median(Price 1, Price 2, Contract Price), where Price 2 = price index + moving average of the basis (basis sampled each second as bid/ask average minus index). From 2025-09-18 08:01 UTC the basis moving-average window shrank from 1 minute (60 points) to 30 seconds (30 points).

The JELLY settlement drew centralization criticism because a validator vote, not autonomous contract logic, set the closing price. Arthur Hayes wrote 'Let's stop pretending Hyperliquid is decentralized' (Decrypt); Arkham said the manual closing price overrode autonomous contracts and showed a central point of control; OneKey said the intervention boundary was undefined beforehand; the community wiki records Bitget's CEO calling it 'FTX 2.0'.

On Jupiter's JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) the JLP pool is the counterparty to every trade. Traders borrow from the pool, profits are paid from it, and losses flow back into it. JLP's virtual price counts pool assets net of the value reserved to pay traders' profits. Jupiter's April 2026 assessment says JLP holders absorb losses during sustained trader profits, and an independent November 2024 analysis agrees.

Binance settles funding every 8 hours (00:00, 08:00, 16:00 UTC) by default. Since 2025-09-18 08:01 UTC its formula divides the bracketed term by 8/N, where N is the contract's settlement interval in hours, so a 4-hour contract settles half the 8-hour-equivalent rate. Binance samples the premium index every 5 seconds (5,760 points per 8 hours) and time-weights the average. An independent paper also describes funding as typically paid every 8 hours.

During the 2025-10-10 cascade Hyperliquid activated ADL on profitable shorts; the Chitra paper's Hyperliquid dataset shows ADL closing about $2.1B of positions in 12 minutes. CoinShares describes Hyperliquid as the major venue that kept stable performance, and says Lighter did not need ADL because its insurance reserves sufficed.

On Sep 20 (2021 per URL slug of other coverage) the Pyth feed on Solana printed BTC at $5,402 while other sources stayed above $40K; the AMC feed spiked to $772. The Defiant excerpt gives no cause. FTI Consulting argues unified (cross-asset) margin is efficient in calm markets because profits offset losses, but under stress it ties portfolios to their weakest assets. It notes a large share of exposure before the 10 October 2025 crash sat on unified-margin venues, and that long-only collateral sell-offs may not be offset by short profits.

Velocity funding is lazy: it updates when a position is opened or closed and again once enough time has passed, with one-hour periods (an update in the first 20 minutes rounds back onto the hour). A market that neither trades nor gets cranked does not advance its cumulative rates; owed funding shows as unrealized P&L and settles at the account's next action in that market.

Velocity, Drift's successor, lists perp taker fees by trailing 30-day volume at each fill, for SOL-PERP, BTC-PERP and ETH-PERP: Regular (<$5M) 6 bps, VIP 1 ($5M to $80M) 5 bps, VIP 2 ($80M to $200M) 4 bps, VIP 3 (>$200M) 2 bps. The maker rebate is 0.25 bps at every tier and needs the post-only flag. Liquidation volume counts toward tiers. Velocity (Drift's successor; the old docs.drift.trade fee URL now answers 307 to docs.velocity.exchange) lists baseline perp taker fees by trailing 30-day volume: Regular 6 bps, VIP1 ($5M-$80M) 5 bps, VIP2 ($80M-$200M) 4 bps, VIP3 (>$200M) 2 bps. The maker rebate is 0.25 bps at every tier, paid only on post-only orders. Liquidation volume counts toward tiers. The page warns rates are admin-settable and per-market rates can differ.

Treat Velocity's published thresholds as defaults, not live state. The oracles page lists 'default thresholds' and carries no date. The contract-tier page says a market's tier is admin-adjustable and should be read from the onchain market account. The guard-rails page says to read the market account for live caps. Insurance cover is per-market, not per-exchange. Lifetime caps on draws from the shared quote fund are tier A $100M, B $1M, C $100K, and $0 for Speculative, Highly Speculative and Isolated. The cap is cumulative across all of a market's bankruptcies. New markets default to Highly Speculative, so they have no cover until promoted. Zero-cover markets go from estate, to the in-transit fee, to the AMM clawback, to socialization among that market's own traders.

Jupiter retunes its price-impact parameters over time. Chaos Labs' 2025-06-03 forum recommendation lists a delta-imbalance threshold of 0.75e6 for SOL, ETH and BTC; the docs' October 2026 parameters give $1.5M for SOL and ETH and $750,000 for wBTC. A fee quoted from any single date can therefore go stale.

To read live margin parameters, query each venue's own data. Hyperliquid's meta info response carries margin table IDs and tiers, and IDs below 50 are single-tier tables whose max leverage equals the ID. To judge a Velocity market's real cover, read the contract tier before the market. Velocity's Risks page says insurance coverage, oracle tolerance, TWAP damping, auction bands and the AMM cutoff all derive from the tier, and that a re-tier changes the insurance cap, confidence tolerance, TWAP band and auction band at once. Routine changes are timelocked, the most dangerous need the cold key, and a cold-tier change carries no notice period. Live values sit in each market account, not in the docs.

To see a Velocity market's real loss waterfall, read live market-account fields, not the docs. The fields are the contract tier, insurance_claim.quote_max_insurance and quote_settled_insurance, fee_ledger.pending_if_fee, bankruptcy_if_floor_pct, and the Insurance Fund vault balance. The docs say tier assignments, caps, floor percentage and fee rates are admin-settable, that a re-tier changes the insurance cap at once, and that routine changes are timelocked while cold-tier changes carry no notice period.

Jupiter's Beta markets (JUP, HYPE, ZEC and stock perps) run on GUM, an orderbook engine separate from the JLP pool. Liquidation triggers at the mark price, and the forced close fills on the orderbook. Whatever collateral remains after loss and fees goes back to the trader, which can be little or nothing in a fast market. The liquidation fee is 0.75% on crypto markets and 1% on stock markets. A position above its first margin tier is liquidated one tier at a time. The docs say 'There is no auto-deleveraging on Beta markets at launch' and describe no insurance fund.

Execution path differs: Binance avoids full liquidation where possible by cancelling open orders and placing one large IOC order to reduce the position; if margin is still short it closes at bankruptcy price and the Insurance Fund or counterparty liquidation takes the remainder. Hyperliquid instead sends full-size market orders to the public book (20% slices only above 100k USDC) and uses the HLP vault, not an insurance fund, as the backstop liquidator. Both key liquidations off a mark price (Binance: funding data plus a spot basket; Hyperliquid: external CEX prices plus book state).

Default interest is 0.03% per day, 0% for pairs such as ETHBTC; the default interval is 8 hours. Hyperliquid tiers maintenance margin by position size: maintenance_margin = notional_position_value * maintenance_margin_rate - maintenance_deduction. The rate is half the initial margin rate at the tier's max leverage, and the deduction keeps total maintenance margin continuous across tiers. On mainnet, BTC drops from 40x to 20x above 150M USDC notional, ETH from 25x to 15x above 100M, and SOL from 20x to 10x above 70M. Binance USDS-M futures use the same shape, with a per-tier rate and a maintenance amount.

Jupiter Perps' JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) accept 1.1x to 250x leverage when opening a position. At 150x or more the trade form warns that small moves can liquidate the position almost instantly and switches off market-order TP/SL. The liquidation formula uses a separate protocol max_lev of 500, so the minimum margin is size/500 (0.2% of size), against 0.4% initial margin at 250x. The docs warn that above 10x, accrued borrow fees move the liquidation price materially, and that there is no margin call.

Hyperliquid sets maintenance margin at half of initial margin at the asset's max leverage; its docs put this at 1.25% for 40x assets up to 16.7% for 3x assets. OtterSec's decompilation of a testnet-synced hl-node binary recovers the same isolated-position threshold, |notional| / (2 x leverage). Binance states its maintenance margin depends on position size, not on the leverage the user selects.

Liquidation penalties differ by venue. On Jupiter JLP markets a liquidated position forfeits all remaining collateral as the liquidation fee. On Jupiter Beta markets the fee is 0.75% (crypto) or 1% (stock) of position value and leftover collateral is returned, though in a fast market 'it can be little or nothing'. Velocity splits a per-market liquidation fee three ways between the liquidator, the insurance fund and the protocol.

Hyperliquid sets maintenance margin at half of the initial margin at the asset's max leverage. That gives 1.25% for 40x assets and 16.7% for 3x assets. A cross position is liquidated when account value, including unrealized PnL, falls below maintenance margin times total open notional. An isolated position follows the same rule using only its own isolated margin and its own notional.

Hyperliquid funding is F = average premium + clamp(interest - premium, -0.05%, +0.05%) with interest fixed at 0.01% per 8 hours. The premium is the impact-price gap to the oracle, sampled every 5 seconds and averaged over the hour; the 8-hour rate is paid hourly at one eighth. HIP-3 perps use a more responsive premium, 0.5 * (impact bid + impact ask) / oracle - 1. The payment is position size * oracle price * rate, so the oracle, not the mark, converts size to notional.

Jupiter's liquidation price formula uses a 500x protocol-level max leverage to set minimum maintenance margin, although the trading maximum is 250x. Accrued borrow fees shift the liquidation price toward the market price over time. If fees exceed collateral minus size/500, a position can be liquidated with no adverse price move.

No official Drift or Velocity page fetched states a maximum leverage figure. The only figure found is a third-party claim that BTC, ETH and SOL perps offer up to 20x, which is unverified. Per-market initial and maintenance margin ratios live in the on-chain PerpMarket account, so the real cap is a per-market parameter.

Accrued fees move a liquidation price toward the market even when the price is flat. Jupiter's formula subtracts close_fee and the accumulated borrow_fee from collateral before comparing with size / max_lev. If fees exceed collateral_size - size / max_lev, the liquidation price passes the entry price and the position can be liquidated without an adverse price move. Jupiter says the effect is largest above 10x and on long holds, and that withdrawing collateral raises leverage and moves the liquidation price toward the market. Hyperliquid liquidates when account equity falls below maintenance margin, which is half of initial margin at max leverage (1.25% for 40x assets up to 16.7% for 3x assets). It first sends market orders for the full position to the order book; leftover collateral stays with the trader. Liquidations use a mark price that blends external CEX prices with Hyperliquid book state.

Drift and Velocity set initial and maintenance margin ratios per perp market, and an admin can change them. Velocity's docs say maximum leverage is the reciprocal of the initial ratio, and the program bounds that ratio between 1.25% (80x) and 100% (1x). An IMF factor raises the required ratio as a position grows. Neodyme's 2024 audit shows BTC-PERP at 1/20 initial and 3/100 maintenance, and Velocity's examples use 5% and 3%. Maintenance therefore sits near 60% of initial, not a fixed 50%.

How far maintenance margin sits below initial margin differs by venue. Hyperliquid sets MM at 50% of IM at max leverage. Jupiter's JLP markets also reach 50% (0.2% MM against 0.4% IM at 250x). Flash's standard crypto setting puts MM at 10% of IM (0.1% against 1% at 100x) and reaches 50% only in Degen Mode at 500x. Drift and Velocity set the two ratios independently per market, and their examples give 60% (3% against 5%). These ratios are derived from the cited parameters; the venues do not state them.

In the audited and archived Drift code, handle_update_perp_bid_ask_twap (the crank that writes bid, ask and mark TWAPs) requires the caller to have at least $1,000 staked in the insurance fund. It builds its estimate from maker accounts the caller supplies, and it ignores resting orders more than 15% from the oracle price (bids below 85% and asks above 115% of it). The Neodyme audit (May 2024) states the same $1,000 stake requirement. Velocity's 2026 docs call the same cranks 'permissionless'.

The mark-TWAP crank is gated, not open. `update_perp_bid_ask_twap` requires a keeper with at least $1,000 staked in the insurance fund because the caller-supplied maker list is trusted (Neodyme, May 2024). Drift PR #2124, merged 2026-03-17, also drops bids more than 15% below and asks more than 15% above the oracle before estimating the mark TWAP; Velocity kept both rules.

Binance and OKX describe staged reduction; Hyperliquid's default is a full-size market order, with 20% slices only above 100k USDC. Binance cancels all open orders, then places one large IOC order to bring the account back into margin compliance. Only if the user is still deficient does Binance close at the bankruptcy price and hand the position to the Insurance Fund, and it charges a clearance fee on the amount liquidated only. OKX partially reduces positions at tier 3 and above, and says the whole margin of a liquidated position is lost.

Binance caps funding at +/-0.75 x maintenance margin ratio for listed major USDS-M symbols and at +/-2% for other USDS-M perpetuals. It may move a contract to 1-hour settlement after a settlement hits the cap or floor, and back to 4 hours after 16 consecutive cycles at or below 0.025% in absolute value. Only the Binance FAQ states these values, and a page summariser produced the extract, so treat them as unverified.

Zeta's retired platform funded its insurance fund from all platform fees, a fixed share of liquidation incentives and an initial seed. The liquidation reward was 65% of maintenance margin, 30% to the liquidator and 35% to the fund. The fund paid when no liquidator stepped in or a liquidated account could not pay the reward. If liquidation and the fund both failed, an over-bankruptcy ratio on withdrawals, AB x DP/(DP+BA), shared the loss across depositors. The Zeta Foundation says the platform was sunset in May 2025, and the docs pages carry no date.

Drift and Velocity set initial and maintenance margin ratios per perp market, and an admin can change them. Velocity says maximum leverage is the reciprocal of the initial ratio, and that the program bounds the ratio between 1.25% (80x) and 100% (1x). An IMF factor raises the required ratio as a position grows: for ordinary users, get_margin_ratio returns the larger of the base ratio and a size-adjusted ratio. A market can also carry separate high-leverage-mode initial and maintenance ratios, which apply to users in high leverage mode.

Maintenance margin is not always half of initial margin. Neodyme's 2024 audit shows Drift BTC-PERP with an initial weight of 1/20 (5%) and a maintenance weight of 3/100 (3%). Zeta's trading specification lists 5% initial and 3% maintenance for SOL, BTC and ETH (20x), and 12.5% and 8% for BNB. Both ratios put maintenance at 60% or more of initial. Hyperliquid and Jupiter's Beta markets set maintenance at half of initial.

Velocity's liquidation engine uses an unbuffered entry test at the maintenance requirement and a 2% of notional exit buffer above maintenance. Margin shortfalls under $50 free immediately, and positions of $50 or less can be taken in full. Liquidation is rejected with PriceBandsBreached when oracle and 5-minute TWAP diverge by 50% or more. Liquidator, insurance-fund and protocol fees are admin-set per market, initialize to zero, and the docs show 0.75% liquidator and 0.75% insurance-fund fees only as an example.

Flash Trade V2 exited beta on 2026-06-29. Venues amortize a premium over different clocks. Hyperliquid and Binance express the premium as an 8-hour rate (Hyperliquid pays one eighth each hour); Drift and Velocity pay 1/24 of the TWAP gap each hour, and Zeta defines its rate per 24 hours. By the formulas, the same sustained 1% premium costs about 3% a day on Hyperliquid or Binance but about 1% a day on Drift, Velocity or Zeta, before caps, offsets and dead zones.

Jupiter's Beta markets run on a separate engine (GUM) with USDC collateral and do not use the JLP pool. Hyperliquid, Binance and OKX all liquidate off a mark price, not the last traded price. Hyperliquid's mark price blends external CEX prices with its own book state. Binance liquidates when the Mark Price hits the position's liquidation price. OKX starts calculating a liquidation price when the maintenance margin ratio is at or below 100%, and bases that price on the mark price.

Velocity's fork has identical constants, and Velocity's docs say max leverage is the reciprocal of the initial ratio, bounded at 1.25% (80x) to 100% (1x), with an IMF factor that cuts leverage as a position grows. Real per-market caps are admin parameters below these bounds.

For HIP-3 (builder-deployed) perps on Hyperliquid, the premium is P = 0.5 x (impact_bid_px + impact_ask_px) / oracle_px - 1, and a per-market funding-rate multiplier scales the result. trade.xyz lists a multiplier of 0.5 for its active markets, an impact notional of 1,000 USDC, and an interest input of 0.01% per 8 hours (0 for EUR, GBP, JPY and KRW markets). These are deployer-set parameters that can change.

Velocity (Drift's docs host after the docs.drift.trade 307 redirect) runs one insurance fund per collateral spot market, each denominated in its own asset. Every perp is quoted and settled in the quote asset, so all perp bad debt draws on the quote market's fund. The fund is 100% staker-owned, with no protocol-owned share.

Queue-based ADL ranks accounts by percentage profit times leverage and closes them in descending order until the shortfall is covered. Both papers say BitMEX, Binance and Hyperliquid use this scheme. Chitra's paper dates it to Huobi in 2015, BitMEX in 2016 and Binance in 2019, and names Drift and Paradex as exceptions that use pro-rata rules. The Columbia paper repeats Chitra's estimate that about 95% of perpetual volume sits on queue-based venues, so that figure rests on one author.

Jupiter Perps' JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) let a trader pick 1.1x to 250x; Jupiter's overview lists 250x as the maximum, $10 minimum collateral and at most 6 open positions. At 150x or more the trade form warns that positions can be liquidated almost instantly and disables market-order take profit and stop loss. Solana Compass independently reports 'up to 250x' on these markets (2026-09-22).

Hyperliquid limits margin removal. Unrealized PnL can leave an isolated position or the cross account only if the remaining margin is at least 10% of total position value and still meets initial margin: transfer_margin_required = max(initial_margin_required, 0.1 * total_position_value). The rule covers withdrawals, transfers to the spot wallet and isolated margin removal. A community wiki repeats the formula.

Velocity grades every oracle read as Valid or one of six failures: non-positive; too volatile (price and running oracle TWAP differ by more than 5x either way); too uncertain (confidence above 2% of price times a per-tier multiplier); stale for margin (default 48 s, 144 s for stablecoin feeds); insufficient data points (Pyth push only); stale for AMM (4 s). The Drift SDK checks them in that precedence order. The values are guard-rail defaults that an admin can change.

Jupiter's beta header shows a 1-hour rate and derives the 8-hour and annualised figures as simple multiples. Jupiter's JLP borrow rate is annual / 8,760. On Hyperliquid, Binance, Velocity, Zeta and Jupiter beta, a positive rate means longs pay shorts.

Velocity caps the funding premium at 3% of oracle TWAP for contract tiers A and B, 5% for tier C and 10% below C. The AMM acts as counterparty to imbalance and may spend at most one third of its retained equity per funding period; the insurance fund is not used to cover funding shortfalls.

In the legacy Drift v2 program source, `update_funding_rate` builds the hourly rate in price units, not as a percentage. Spread = mark mid-TWAP minus oracle TWAP, plus an offset of |oracle TWAP| / 5000, clamped to +/- oracle TWAP / 33 for contract tiers A and B (about 3%), / 20 for tier C (5%) and / 10 below C (10%), then multiplied by FUNDING_RATE_BUFFER (1000) and divided by 24 for a one-hour funding period. On Drift the mark price that funding uses is a bid/ask TWAP pair, not a last-trade price: mark mid-TWAP = (bid TWAP + ask TWAP) / 2 over the funding period. Samples arrive by two paths: the `update_perp_bid_ask_twap` crank, which estimates best bid and ask at an impact depth of open interest / 1000 (clamped to 100 to 5000 times the minimum order size) from maker accounts the caller supplies, and an AMM-spread estimate taken at each funding update. Each new sample is clamped to within 10% (tier A), 20% (B), 50% (C) or 33% (other tiers) of the current TWAP.

The legacy Drift program's IDL lists 249 instructions and none is an auto-deleveraging instruction. The engine instructions are the liquidate_* family, resolve_perp_pnl_deficit, resolve_perp_bankruptcy, resolve_spot_bankruptcy, settle_revenue_to_insurance_fund and the insurance-fund stake instructions. Neodyme's 2024 instruction list matches. A text search of the Velocity liquidation, insurance and admin modules found no 'deleverag' string. Drift and Velocity therefore share loss by a funding-rate charge, not by closing winners.

Jupiter's liquidation page defines max_lev in its formula as the 'protocol-level maximum leverage: 500', distinct from the 250x trading maximum. The minimum margin is size/500 (0.2% of position size). Liquidation price = price -/+ ((collateral_size - close_fee - borrow_fee - size/max_lev) x price / size). If fees exceed collateral_size - size/max_lev, the liquidation price moves past entry, so a position can be liquidated with no adverse price move.

Velocity (the Drift v2 fork; docs.drift.trade now 307-redirects to docs.velocity.exchange) sets the hourly funding rate from 1/24 of (market_twap - oracle_twap) / oracle_twap, where market TWAP is the midpoint of the bid and ask TWAPs. The docs apply a per-market dead zone and an offset floor of oracle TWAP / 3333 (about 10.95% annualized) before the hourly conversion.

Mark TWAP can be moved cheaply when the crank trusts quotes that never had to survive a fill. Velocity's code cites OtterSec finding #146: a caller could place a self-crossed pair of quotes, crank, and cancel in one transaction, moving the mark TWAP that sets a third party's forced-close auction band. The fix is BID_ASK_TWAP_MIN_QUOTE_REST (9,600 ms of on-chain rest before a quote counts) plus pausing the crank while a market's funding is paused. Legacy Drift master has no such constant.

Jupiter's liquidation formula uses a separate 500x protocol-level max_lev, not the 250x selectable maximum. The minimum margin is size/500, which is 0.2% of position size. Liquidation price = price -/+ ((collateral - close_fee - borrow_fee - size/max_lev) * price / size), so accumulated fees can push the liquidation price past entry with no adverse price move.

Flash Trade's docs (as of 2026-07-03) list open/close fees of 0.02% for crypto-pool majors (SOL, BTC, ETH, ZEC, BNB), Gold-pool markets (forex, metals, commodities), equities (AMD 0.05%) and HYPE; 0.1% for JUP, JTO and memes; 0.2% for KMNO and PYTH; and 0.5% for ORE. The confidence tolerance is 2% of price times a tier multiplier: tier A 2%, B 2%, C 4%, Speculative 20%, Highly Speculative 100%, Isolated 100% (multipliers 1, 1, 2, 10, 50, 50). Velocity's contract-tier page, its oracles page and the Drift SDK's getMaxConfidenceIntervalMultiplier agree.

Data access differs and shapes every cross-venue comparison. Hyperliquid's liquidation and ADL fills are public on-chain data: Chitra's reconstruction uses its on-chain fill log, and CoinDesk counted liquidated wallets from Hyperliquid's public leaderboard. Chitra states that account-level data on Binance's ADL use is not public, and Binance's documented liquidation stream keeps only the latest liquidation order per symbol in each 1000 ms window. Venue-level comparisons of liquidation volume or ADL use are therefore exact for Hyperliquid and bounded estimates for Binance.

Jupiter Perps launched Chaos Labs' Edge oracle (announced 2024-09-12) as its price source in place of a 'legacy oracle architecture'. Jupiter's current docs list Edge as primary, with Chainlink and Pyth for verification and fallback.

Scoping check: a Morpho user blamed an 'easily manipulated' Pyth cbETH feed for a 2025-03-02 liquidation. The market curator Re7 Labs, reviewing with Pyth, said it was not manipulation: the cbETH/WETH market (94.5% LLTV) read two separate Pyth push feeds updated by an off-chain scheduler, its oracle does not check price timestamps, and ETH/USD updated to $2,405.22 at 16:39:33 UTC while cbETH/USD stayed at $2,538.33, skewing the ratio from 1.091 to 1.055. About 14 ETH was liquidated across three positions. This was push, not a stale pull feed.

If |spread| is inside the market's fundingClampThreshold (bps of the oracle TWAP; docs example 5 bps), the premium is dropped and only the floor remains. Beyond the band, (|spread| - threshold) x fundingRampSlope is added to the floor. The floor is oracle TWAP / 3333 (about 10.95% a year, 0.00125% an hour). Velocity grades each oracle sample and lets each action decide which grades it accepts. The funding update accepts only Valid, stale-for-AMM, insufficient-data-points and stale-for-margin samples. It rejects non-positive samples, samples more than 5x or less than 1/5 of the running oracle TWAP (too volatile), and samples whose confidence exceeds 2% of price times the market's tier multiplier (too uncertain).

Zeta's docs define funding as impactMidpoint / oracle - 1 per 24 hours, where impactMidpoint is the order-book midpoint given $1,000 of quotes on each side; payment is rate * oracle * position size, calculated about every 10 seconds and applied lazily on balance-sensitive actions and by cranks. The page was last updated about two years before 2026-11-06 and Zeta's original platform was sunset in May 2025 (see the venue-status concept), so treat it as historical.

XRP: 20x up to 40M, 10x above. A 21-asset group that includes HYPE, DOGE and ZEC: 10x up to 20M, 5x above. A group that includes JUP, BNB and PAXG: 10x up to 3M, 5x above. Jupiter JLP borrow fees accrue hourly on the full position size without compounding, from a per-asset utilization curve (annual rate rising from a minimum to a target, then steeply to a maximum, divided by 8,760). Longs use the market asset's utilization and shorts use the USDC custody's. The docs' illustration is $3.84 per day on a $10,000 position at 0.0016% per hour. JLP holders earn 75% of fees from JLP-market trading, swaps and JLP mint/burn.

Velocity measures distance to liquidation as health = 100 * (1 - maintenance margin requirement / total collateral), using maintenance-weighted collateral. An account becomes liquidatable at health 0. Liquidation starts partial and aims for the maintenance requirement plus a 2% buffer. In the program, MarginContext carries a margin_buffer, and cross and isolated calculations have separate exit checks (can_exit_cross_margin_liquidation and can_exit_isolated_margin_liquidation).

Each Drift-lineage perp market has a contract tier that caps its lifetime draws on the shared quote-asset (USDC) insurance fund. An admin may set a market's own cap at or below its ceiling, never above. The market's remaining claim is quote_max_insurance minus quote_settled_insurance. Both resolvers add each draw to the settled amount, so the cap covers all of a market's bankruptcies together, not each one.

Velocity splits each taker fee after four amounts come off the top: a referee discount, a filler reward (the lesser of 10% of the fee and a time-based amount starting at one cent), a referrer reward of 10% or 20%, and the maker rebate. The remainder goes to the AMM, the insurance fund and the protocol; mainnet's live configuration is 15%, 15% and 70%, all admin-settable. A builder fee is charged on top and does not change the taker tier.

Hyperliquid and Binance use the same funding skeleton: F = average premium index + clamp(interest rate - premium index, -0.05%, +0.05%). Hyperliquid fixes interest at 0.01% per 8 hours, samples the premium every 5 seconds, and pays hourly at one eighth of the 8-hour rate. Binance, from 2025-09-18 08:01 UTC, divides the result by 8/N (N = settlement interval in hours) so 4-hour contracts scale correctly.

Binance publishes governance rules for its insurance funds. The minimum balance is calibrated to a 99.9% confidence interval plus historical stress scenarios, which Binance says is unrelated to how often ADL occurs, and Binance reviews it quarterly. When a fund is insufficient, Binance says it will contribute additional assets and the ADL mechanism will be engaged. Each fund has a confidential Maximum Takeover Capacity, defined as a multiple of its balance. Binance may deploy funds above the minimum for other purposes and says the funds are not insurance products.

Chitra's v3 reconstruction of Hyperliquid on 2025-10-10 reports an aggregate loser deficit of about $100.1M, a 'needed' haircut budget of about $15.1M, and production ADL wealth removed from winners of about $60.1M, an overshoot of about $45.0M that rises to $51.7M under longer evaluation horizons. A stylized equity-space queue diagnostic gives about $653.6M, about 6.66x the PnL figure because winners were overcollateralized. The method is a public-data two-pass no-ADL replay, not a ledger.

Do not quote Chitra's $650M as dollars ADL took from winners. v1 (2025-11-30) claimed about 8x and $630M of unnecessary haircuts; v2 (2025-12-08) claimed about 28x and $653M; v3 (2026-02-16) moved haircuts from equity to PnL after public critique and reports $45.0M to $51.7M of excess profit lost. A companion paper, 'Autodeleveraging as Online Learning' (arXiv 2602.15182, 16 Feb 2026; Chitra, Thogiti and two co-authors), models ADL as haircuts to positive P&L, not seizure of collateral. Its public-data replay finds Hyperliquid's production ADL overshot by $45.0M to $51.7M on 10 Oct 2025, and its best counterfactual algorithm cuts the overshoot to about $3M. The two papers share a lead author, so they are not independent confirmations of each other.

JLP holders receive 75% of all fees from the JLP markets (opening and closing fees, price impact, borrow fees, swap fees); the other 25% goes to Jupiter as protocol revenue. JLP holders are the counterparty to every JLP-market trade, so trader profits are paid from the pool. Jupiter's Beta markets do not use the pool.

Velocity splits each taker fee in a fixed order. It first removes the referee discount (5% of the gross fee, never collected), the referrer reward (10% or 20% by referrer level), the filler reward (the lesser of 10% of the fee and a time-based amount that starts at one cent) and the maker rebate (0.25 bps); the referral legs pay out only while builder codes are enabled. It then divides the remainder 15% to the AMM, 15% to the insurance fund and 70% to the protocol on mainnet today. The docs call the AMM and insurance shares admin-settable. Spot fills and swaps charge no trading fee.

One new oracle sample can move a market's running oracle TWAP by at most a per-tier band: 10% for tier A, 20% for B, 50% for C and about 33% for Speculative, Highly Speculative and Isolated. The bands are not monotonic, because tier C is wider than the tail tiers. A large genuine move therefore takes several intervals to enter the TWAP, and the divergence bands stay tight meanwhile.

The CEX-style clamp makes funding flat for small premiums. With F = P + clamp(I - P, -0.05%, +0.05%) and I = 0.01%, any premium between -0.04% and +0.06% gives F = I exactly; Binance uses the identical form. Velocity's explicit dead zone plus fixed offset produces the same flat band with a per-market width. Small mark-oracle gaps therefore do not move funding on any of these venues. This is derived from the formulas, not stated by the sources.

Drift and Velocity price liquidations at the oracle price, not the mark price, and block them when the oracle diverges 50% or more from its 5-minute TWAP (error PriceBandsBreached in Velocity). Both liquidate in parts: a throttle limits how much of the shortfall can close at once, and the engine targets a buffer above maintenance margin so the account is not liquidated again on the next tick.

When liquidation cannot close a losing account in time, Drift, Velocity and Zeta cover the bad debt in a fixed order: the account's own collateral, then an insurance fund, then a loss-sharing step. They differ at the last step. Drift and Velocity charge every open position in the market through the funding rate. Zeta's retired design cut every depositor's withdrawal. Drift's docs call the insurance fund 'the first backstop' for bankruptcies.

Initial margin (IM) gates actions that add risk. Maintenance margin (MM) is a lower line that triggers liquidation. Between the two lines an account keeps its positions but cannot add risk, which stops a position being opened straight into liquidation. Velocity's docs assign IM to opening positions, withdrawals and risk-increasing orders, and MM to liquidation only. Neodyme's 2024 audit describes the same split for Drift. Hyperliquid derives IM from the leverage the user picks and liquidates below MM.

Jupiter Perps keeps collateral on each position in its JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC). A long posts the traded asset and a short posts USDC, and the collateral token cannot change after opening. Jupiter's JLP-market pages never use the words cross or isolated. Jupiter does not issue margin calls.

Velocity keeps a standing first-loss tranche so a permissionless fee sweep cannot drain the in-transit insurance fee to zero. The default floor is 10 bps of open-interest notional, priced at the market's oracle TWAP (DEFAULT_BANKRUPTCY_IF_FLOOR_PCT; BANKRUPTCY_IF_FLOOR_DISABLED turns it off). Once a bankruptcy is latched against a market, the sweep withholds the whole in-transit fee, and delisting is blocked until the claim clears. On a market with $50M of open interest the default floor is $50,000, small beside the $1M tier B cap.

Hyperliquid ADL triggers when an account or isolated position value goes negative, ranks opposite profitable positions by (mark/entry) x (notional/account value), and closes them at the previous mark price; its ADL docs page does not mention an insurance fund.

Zeta's documented backstop had three layers. A liquidator takes the position. The insurance fund, made of platform fees, a fixed share of liquidation incentives and an initial seed, pays when no liquidator steps in or the liquidated account cannot fund the reward. If both fail, the over-bankruptcy loss is shared across all depositors by scaling withdrawals by DP/(DP+BA), where DP is deposits to the platform and BA is the bankruptcy amount. The Zeta Foundation page says Zeta Protocol would cease operations in May 2025, so this is a historical design.

Bad debt on Solana venues comes from liquidations that cannot execute in time. Neodyme names 'sudden extreme market movements or chain congestion' as the cause of excess losses on Drift. Velocity's Risks page says congestion or a validator incident means liquidations do not land, and 'there is no protocol-side guard rail for this'. On 2022-11-10 the lender Solend reported over $6M of bad debt on a roughly $8M USDC loan backed by about $2M of SOL after liquidations ran slowly; its DAO treasury covered the loss. Solend is a lending protocol, not a perp venue.

Unstaking from an Insurance Fund takes at least 13 days. The default cooldown is set per spot market, and legacy Drift v2 has the same THIRTEEN_DAY default. A request freezes the share value. At completion the payout is the smaller of the frozen value and the current value, so gains after the request do not reach the staker but a bankruptcy draw during the cooldown does. Neodyme describes the same smaller-of rule. Completion also fails while the spot market's utilization or its TWAP is above 90%. Request and completion both fail with ExchangePaused when withdrawals are paused exchange-wide.

Drift and Velocity classify every oracle read into one of six failure grades, or Valid: non-positive (any price field at or below zero), too volatile (price and the running oracle TWAP differ by more than 5x up, or down to one fifth), too uncertain (confidence wider than 2% of price times the market's tier multiplier), stale for margin, insufficient data points, and stale for the AMM (with immediate and low-risk sub-levels). The protocol does not decide which fault is happening. Each action decides which grades it accepts.

Velocity keeps a standing first-loss tranche so a permissionless fee sweep cannot drain it. Each market holds back a floor of its in-transit insurance fee, by default 0.1% of open-interest notional priced at the oracle TWAP. When a bankruptcy latches, the sweep withholds the whole in-transit fee, and delisting is blocked until the claim clears. On a market with $50,000,000 of open interest the default floor is $50,000.

On Hyperliquid, the margin needed to open a position is position_size * mark_price / leverage. The user picks an integer leverage from 1 up to the asset's maximum. The exchange checks leverage only when the position opens, so the user must monitor it afterwards. Initial margin on a cross position cannot be withdrawn. Isolated margin can be added or removed after opening, and an isolated position applies its own unrealized PnL as extra margin to itself.

An independent academic paper, 'Risk-Based Auto-Deleveraging' (Campbell, Hey, Moallemi, Nutz; arXiv 2603.15963, v1 16 March 2026, v2 16 July 2026), finds a different optimum. For one asset with isolated margin, a minimax-leverage policy is optimal for all monotone risk measures: it cuts the most levered accounts first, then equalizes leverage. The authors say it clarifies the logic of queue-based mechanisms used in practice. Applied to the 10 October 2025 Hyperliquid event, their allocations achieve lower expected shortfall than the realized allocation.

Anyone can resolve a latched bankruptcy in Velocity. A solvency flag, separate from the withdraw pauses and flipped only by the cold-admin key, gates resolution. Perp bankruptcies must resolve before spot ones (error PerpBankruptcyMustPrecedeSpot) because both draw the same quote insurance vault. The code comment says a caller-chosen order would shift loss between perp stakers and spot depositors, and credits audit finding #52.

The Drift oracle layer was not the root cause. Nexus Mutual calls the CVT oracle manipulation 'a downstream effect of the key compromise, not an independent failure of Drift's oracle system'. Neither mode is strictly safer. Isolated margin caps a position's loss at its allocated margin but gives it a closer liquidation price. Cross margin pushes liquidation further away by drawing on the whole account, but it puts the whole account at risk. Hyperliquid's docs match the mechanics: an isolated liquidation price depends on the leverage set, a cross one does not. Athenum (June 2026) says 'Neither is safer in the abstract', and OneKey (May 2026) says cross is not automatically safer.

Hyperliquid withdrawal or transfer of unrealized PnL from an isolated position or the cross account is limited by transfer_margin_required = max(initial_margin_required, 0.1 * total_position_value). Some assets are 'strict isolated', which adds a constraint that isolated margin cannot be removed. HIP-3 DEXs also support a 'no cross' mode.

Which positions share cross margin on Hyperliquid depends on the account abstraction. Under a unified account or portfolio margin, cross positions in HIP-3 DEXs that use the same collateral share margin. Under the standard abstraction, cross margin applies to each DEX separately. HIP-3 DEXs can also offer a 'no cross' mode that allows isolated margin with margin removal but no cross margin. Some assets are 'strict isolated': margin cannot be removed and is released in proportion as the position closes.

HIP-3 DEXs can offer a no-cross mode that allows isolated margin with margin removal. Which positions share cross margin depends on the account abstraction. Velocity blocks P&L settlement when oracle-to-TWAP divergence or oracle-to-mark standard deviation exceeds a per-tier limit: 50 bp and 200 bp for tiers A and B, 100 bp and 500 bp for C, 250 bp and 1,000 bp for Speculative and the tail tiers. The page says half a percent of oracle drift stops settlement on a tier A market.

Median and weighted-median designs raise the cost of moving a price but did not stop manipulation or anomalies that arrived through a trusted input. JELLY pushed a heavily weighted CEX market (Bybit). The SK Hynix print passed through the HIP-3 oracle into two of the three mark inputs. A vendor page that says a composite mark price 'eliminates single-venue dependency' (Block Scholes, 2026-04-09) names no incident, weights or test.

Binance's 2025-10-10 failure was collateral pricing, not its liquidation sequence. Its unified account marked USDe, BNSOL and WBETH from its own order book; USDe traded near $0.65 on Binance while staying near $1 elsewhere, and the markdowns pushed accounts under maintenance margin. Binance paid about $283M to users who held those assets as collateral between 21:36 and 22:16 UTC. Ethena's founder said the dislocation was isolated to one venue that referenced its own order book.

Transaction submitters choose which signed update to include, which is functionally equivalent to latency: they can see a later price before using an earlier one.
