Jupiter's pages for the JLP markets describe no insurance fund, no bad-debt waterfall, no socialized-loss rule and no ADL. A text search of the liquidation page, JLP FAQ, JLP overview, Perps FAQ, positions page and technical reference, and a read of the April 2026 JLP risk report, found none of these terms; the only loss absorber they name is the pool itself. Silence in documentation does not prove the program has no such mechanism, and the program code was not checked.

Before the exploit, Drift's docs gave a shorter order: the external USDC insurance fund up to the market's limit, then 'internal insurance' (the vAMM's lifetime profit for that market), then a pro-rata socialized loss across all open positions in that market. The drift-labs/protocol-v2 resolve_perp_bankruptcy code does the same: insurance fund, then the AMM fee pool, then a cumulative-funding-rate bump. Neodyme's 2024 audit says insurance funds cover excess losses and 'only when they are depleted is any remaining debt socialized'.

Solana's slot time is dropping from 400 ms to 200 ms in steps, so a fixed slot-count staleness window shrinks in wall-clock time by up to 2x. Velocity stores the live slot length in State and states its oracle windows in wall-clock time (4 s for the AMM, 48 s for margin), flooring conversions for risk ceilings. Drift v2 source comments assume about 5 s and 60 s for the same 10-slot and 120-slot defaults.

ADL trigger and closing price differ. Binance calls ADL the final step, used only if the Futures Insurance Funds cannot accept a bankrupt position, and closes profitable positions at the bankrupt order's bankruptcy price. OKX triggers ADL when its security fund falls well below a preset threshold, normally closes deleveraged positions at the mark price, and switches to bankruptcy price if the fund is nearly depleted. Hyperliquid triggers ADL when an account or isolated position value goes negative and closes at the previous mark price, with no insurance-fund step documented.

Drift's program computes three margin requirement types: Initial, Fill and Maintenance. In perp_market.rs, get_margin_ratio returns the initial ratio for Initial, the maintenance ratio for Maintenance, and the average of the two for Fill. Neodyme's 2024 audit and Velocity's docs describe the same split: Initial gates risk-increasing orders, Fill gates the check on a risk-increasing fill, and Maintenance gates liquidation.

The pre-exploit Drift v2 program had a shorter perp waterfall. Its resolve_perp_bankruptcy drew first on the quote Insurance Fund vault, limited by quote_max_insurance minus quote_settled_insurance and by the vault balance minus one token. It then drew on the market's AMM fee pool, up to every token in that pool, and socialized the rest. It had no estate-setoff step and no in-transit-fee tranche. Velocity added both and limited the AMM tranche to the fee provision the AMM had received. The app picks per action between request-and-fulfillment (the trader submits a request transaction, a keeper validates it and submits a second execution transaction; limit and TP/SL orders execute this way) and a single transaction co-signed by a Jupiter keeper (closing from jup.ag by default). On the request path the trade is not live until the keeper's fulfillment confirms. Velocity measures distance to liquidation as health = 100 * (1 - maintenance margin requirement / total collateral), using maintenance-weighted collateral. The account is liquidatable at health 0. The Initial view uses stricter weights and gates new risk, so free collateral can look usable on the Maintenance view while the Initial check rejects a new position. Positive unsettled P&L is weighted per market, starting at 0 for initial margin and 100% for maintenance, and a $100 per-position ceiling limits how much of it counts toward initial margin.

It is a forecast; the settled rate is fixed at the hourly update.

Velocity's perp bankruptcy waterfall runs in a fixed order. Tranche 2 is the shared quote-market Insurance Fund vault, limited by the market's remaining insurance cap and by the vault balance minus one token. Tranche 3 is a clawback of the AMM fee provision. Velocity applies a different set of acceptable validity grades per action: AMM fills need Valid (or a low-risk stale grade); margin and orderbook fills reject non-positive, too volatile, too uncertain and stale-for-margin; liquidation rejects only non-positive and too volatile. Staleness stops AMM quoting at 4 s and margin/orderbook fills at 48 s, while liquidations and trigger orders keep running. The docs warn that wide confidence bands can leave a position unliquidatable during a genuine dislocation.

Hyperliquid's mark price takes external CEX prices as an input, so a squeeze on thin CEX or spot markets can move its liquidation prices. In the JELLY attack, CoinGecko, the community docs and Rekt report the price was pushed across Hyperliquid and other exchanges, which let the liquidated short reach HLP.

Hyperliquid documents a computeUnifiedAccountRatio function for monitoring liquidation risk. For each collateral token it divides the summed crossMaintenanceMarginUsed by the spot balance minus the isolated margin used, then takes the maximum ratio. Isolated positions therefore reduce the balance available to back cross positions in a unified account.

The confidence limit scales with the market's contract tier. The Drift SDK multiplies the 2% base by 1 for tiers A and B, 2 for C, 10 for Speculative and 50 for Highly Speculative and Isolated. Velocity's docs say 1x on tier A up to 50x, so the tail tiers tolerate a band up to 100% of price before a sample is graded too uncertain.

Velocity's docs list two supported oracle sources, Pyth Lazer and Pyth push, and say the Switchboard and Pyth pull variants are 'deprecated and rejected onchain'. The source is set per market. A Pyth Lazer price is not written by Pyth's own crank: a keeper relays a signed message onchain and the program verifies the publisher's signature before use.

The Drift attack was an access and operations compromise, not a smart-contract bug or stolen key. The attacker used Solana durable nonces to keep pre-signed transactions valid for weeks, obtained two approvals on the 2-of-5 Security Council multisig, and on 2026-04-01 (about a minute after a legitimate insurance-fund test withdrawal) submitted transactions that created and executed a malicious admin transfer. Drift's relaunch design disables durable nonces, adds timelocks on critical actions, and moves core assets to a new community-governed multisig.

Binance USDS-M futures sets initial margin by the leverage the user selects. Maintenance margin is Notional Position Value * Maintenance Margin Rate - Maintenance Amount, using tiered brackets where larger positions get higher rates. In isolated mode an open position's leverage cannot be reduced, whereas in cross mode it can be adjusted.

Binance USDS-M futures derive initial margin from the leverage the user selects. With an open position in isolated mode the user cannot reduce its leverage, while in cross mode leverage can be adjusted. The support article was updated on 2026-03-27, warns it may be outdated, and shows its tier tables only as images.

On Binance USDS-M futures, initial margin is determined by the leverage the user selects, and larger positions get lower maximum leverage. With an open position in cross margin mode the user can increase or decrease leverage. With an open position in isolated margin mode the user cannot reduce leverage. The support article was updated on 2026-03-27.

It does not confirm any later parameter change. Treat uncapped single-asset backstop exposure as a design risk unless current docs state otherwise.

Auto-deleveraging (ADL) is a last-resort loss-socialization mechanism for perpetual futures venues. It runs when liquidations fail to keep the venue solvent and other loss-absorbing resources, such as the insurance fund, cannot cover the shortfall. The venue then forcibly reduces the positions of solvent traders on the other side, at prices that leave the venue solvent. Two separate research groups give this definition: Gauntlet's Tarun Chitra and a Columbia University team.

POPCAT (Nov 12, 2025), per on-chain analysts (MLMabc, Lookonchain): a trader moved $3M USDC from OKX into 19 wallets, built a roughly $26M-$30M POPCAT long behind a roughly $20M buy wall near $0.21, cancelled the wall, and was liquidated within seconds. The position passed to HLP, which lost about $4.9M (under 1% of TVL per CoinGecko); the attacker's $3M was wiped out. Hyperliquid paused deposits and withdrawals for about an hour but issued no statement tying the pause to POPCAT, and no official postmortem was found; the loss figure is not confirmed by Hyperliquid.

Drift v2's constants.rs sets a general floor of 125 / 10,000 (1.25% initial margin, 80x) as MIN_MARGIN_RATIO and a lower floor of 50 / 10,000 (0.5%, 200x) as HIGH_LEVERAGE_MIN_MARGIN_RATIO for a high-leverage mode. Velocity's docs restate the 1.25% (80x) bound for its forked program and describe no high-leverage mode in the pages read. The bounds limit what an admin can set. They are not the leverage users see: Velocity's live caps are 20x and 10x.

Drift and Velocity use three margin requirement types: Initial, Fill and Maintenance. In the program, get_margin_ratio returns the initial ratio for Initial, the maintenance ratio for Maintenance, and the midpoint of the two for Fill. The Fill check runs after a fill that increases the taker's risk. A fill that reduces risk is checked at Maintenance. Neodyme's 2024 audit and Velocity's docs describe the same rules.

Drift v2's insurance code carries the limits that the v1 post-mortem said were missing. Each perp market has a lifetime insurance cap bounded by its tier, a per-period revenue-withdraw limit, and an unrealized-P&L imbalance threshold. The post-mortem section that proposes the v2 fixes was not in the fetched text, so the link between the two is an inference.

Both venues trigger liquidation on a mark price, not the last trade. Hyperliquid's docs say its liquidation mark price combines external CEX prices with Hyperliquid's own book state, so it can differ materially from the book price in volatile periods; Binance liquidates when the Mark Price hits the liquidation price. Mark-price construction is therefore a shared input risk, and the Oct 10, 2025 Binance failure was in the reference prices feeding collateral valuation, not in the trigger rule.

Jupiter's selection logic: use Edge if it is not stale and within a threshold of both Chainlink and Pyth. Otherwise compare Chainlink and Pyth and use the more recent if they agree within the threshold. If two or more oracles fail, the price does not update. The docs give no threshold value and do not say which price drives liquidations or take-profit and stop-loss triggers. Prices update during trade execution and through a separate keeper.

Whatever the book cannot absorb is inherited by the HLP liquidator vault, which becomes the counterparty of last resort. The Columbia paper (Campbell, Hey, Moallemi, Nutz; arXiv 2603.15963, 16 Mar 2026) optimizes for the exchange. In a single-asset isolated-margin model with a risk-neutral loss objective, the unique optimal ADL policy minimizes the maximum leverage among participants. Positions of the most highly levered accounts are reduced first, and leverage is equalized by a water-filling rule. The paper calls the policy distribution-free, wash-trade resistant, Sybil resistant and path-independent, and says it clarifies the logic of queue-based mechanisms. Pyth's remediation after the 2021 incident was new aggregation weights derived from relative price differences, an integration test protocol with statistical sanity checks for publishers, better mainnet monitoring, and guidance that protocols use both price and confidence. Pyth's current best-practices page still tells integrators to handle wide confidence by using the EMA price or pausing new activity above a threshold.

ADL is a last-resort loss-socialization mechanism: when liquidations fail to keep the exchange solvent, profitable positions are forcibly reduced to cover the deficit. Gauntlet's paper argues an ADL policy faces a trilemma among exchange solvency, revenue and trader fairness, and that moral hazard grows with participation so zero-loss socialization is impossible.

In every funding formula examined (Hyperliquid, Binance, Velocity, Zeta), the reference leg is an external oracle or index price and the perp leg comes from the venue's own order book (impact prices at a fixed notional, or a bid/ask TWAP). 'Mark price' means different things: Hyperliquid and Binance define it as a median of several inputs used for margin, liquidation and PnL, and do not use it as the funding perp leg. Velocity uses 'mark TWAP' for the bid/ask midpoint TWAP, which is the funding perp leg.

Jupiter's GUM-engine beta markets (JUP, HYPE, ZEC and stock perps) charge hourly funding instead of a borrow fee. Funding accrues while a position is open and is applied every hour on the hour (UTC); a positive rate means longs pay shorts. The mark price is an oracle price (Chainlink for the stock markets) used for margin, PnL and liquidation, and a beta position is liquidated when the mark price reaches its liquidation price. The docs publish no funding formula, cap or reference price for these markets.

A perpetual has no expiry or delivery, so nothing in the contract forces its price to track the underlying. Funding and margin both need a reference price the exchange does not produce. Velocity's docs add that the exchange's own last price is the one number a trader can move, so each market carries an oracle account, written by someone other than the trader, that holds a price, a confidence interval and a timestamp. Margin, liquidation, funding and the AMM quote are all measured against it. Pyth's perps use-case page says oracle prices enter the funding-rate calculation and that the mark pric

All three venues rank ADL candidates by a profit-times-leverage score. Binance ranks profitable positions by PNL% x effective leverage, where effective leverage is abs(notional) / (account balance + unrealized profit). OKX ranks by unrealized PnL% divided by the account-level maintenance margin ratio. Hyperliquid's docs rank by (mark price / entry price) x (notional / account value). Chitra traces the profit-times-leverage queue to BitMEX in 2016 (ADL itself to Huobi in 2015) and says it persists on virtually every centralized exchange and on Hyperliquid.

Jupiter's GUM-powered beta markets (JUP, HYPE, ZEC and stock perps) charge funding instead of a borrow fee. It accrues while the position is open and is applied every hour on the hour (UTC); the app shows a one-hour rate, and the 8-hour and annualized displays are simple multiples of it. Mark price is an oracle price (Chainlink for the stock markets) used for margin, PnL and liquidation, while the chart shows the last traded price. No funding formula, cap or price basis is published.

Hyperliquid backstop liquidation: below 2/3 of maintenance margin the HLP liquidator vault can take over. A cross backstop transfers all cross positions and cross margin (the trader can end with zero equity); an isolated backstop transfers only that isolated position and margin. The maintenance margin is not returned to the user during a backstop, and backstop pnl goes to HLP depositors rather than the exchange operator.

Velocity's guard-rails page describes two directionless divergence checks against the 5-minute oracle TWAP. The 10% band (whichever of the AMM price or live oracle sits further from the TWAP) reverts with PriceBandsBreached and blocks PnL settlement, perp PnL deficit resolution and the PnL pool's fee sweep. The 50% band (live oracle vs TWAP) makes order fills return without filling and reverts post-fill checks, stop and take-profit triggers, all four liquidation paths and swap settlement. During a genuine oracle dislocation a position can therefore be neither closed by its owner nor liquidated

On Jupiter's JLP markets, leverage runs from 1.1x to 250x, so initial margin at the maximum is 0.4% of position size. The liquidation formula uses a protocol max_lev of 500, which sets minimum margin at size / 500, or 0.2% of size. The docs say the 500x figure defines minimum maintenance margin and differs from the 250x opening cap. Close fees and accrued borrow fees reduce collateral in the formula before it is compared with that minimum. A liquidation takes all remaining collateral as a liquidation fee.

Hyperliquid tiers maintenance margin by position size with a CEX-style formula: maintenance_margin = notional_position_value * maintenance_margin_rate - maintenance_deduction. The tier rate is half the initial margin rate at that tier's max leverage. The deduction accumulates across tiers so total maintenance margin stays continuous as size grows. Binance USDS-M futures documents the same shape: Maintenance Margin = Notional Position Value * Maintenance Margin Rate - Maintenance Amount, with rates set per notional tier.

On Hyperliquid, premium = impact_price_difference / oracle_price, where impact_price_difference = max(impact_bid_px - oracle_px, 0) - max(oracle_px - impact_ask_px, 0). HIP-3 perps use a more responsive premium, (0.5 * (impact_bid_px + impact_ask_px) / oracle_px) - 1. The funding payment is position_size * oracle_price * funding_rate: the spot oracle price, not the mark price, converts size to notional.

The loss-absorbing layer differs. On Binance the exchange runs the matched book, and its Futures Insurance Funds (topped up by Binance) take over bankrupt positions before ADL. On Hyperliquid the HLP vault, open to anyone holding USDC on Hyperliquid and charging no performance fee, warehouses backstop-liquidated inventory, so HLP depositors receive both the profits and the losses of backstop liquidations. Chitra's paper describes HLP vaults as holding directional exposure on behalf of liquidity providers, a hybrid of an order-book venue and an inventory-taking pool.

Neither the legacy Drift v2 program nor Velocity's velocity-v1 program contains an auto-deleveraging path. A text search of both liquidation and insurance modules for 'deleverag' and 'adl' returned nothing on 2026-11-06. Perp residual loss is spread over all open interest by the funding-rate bump, and spot residual loss by a lower deposit-interest index. This differs from ADL: no position is force-closed, and the charge falls on both sides of the book per unit of base, so a trader on the winning side also pays. The beta-markets page publishes no formula, no cap, and does not say which price funding uses; mark price there is an oracle price (Chainlink for stock markets).

Venue designs differ on the perp-side measure that funding compares with the oracle: Hyperliquid uses an impact-price premium sampled every 5 seconds, Velocity uses a bid/ask-midpoint TWAP gap with a dead zone, and Zeta uses an impact midpoint at $1000 quote depth. All three measure the gap against an oracle price, not against a mark price.

The party that absorbs liquidation failure differs. At centralized exchanges the exchange creates the complementary positions, so bad debt falls on its insurance fund and balance sheet. On Hyperliquid, HLP depositors own the offsetting inventory and absorb manipulation losses, as JELLY and POPCAT showed. Hyperliquid's docs present this as a feature, because HLP depositors rather than the operator receive backstop liquidation profit.

Both Drift-lineage codebases socialize a perp residual by dividing it by the market's total open base (absolute long base plus absolute short base), adding the result to the long cumulative funding rate and subtracting it from the short rate. Every open position pays per unit of base, once, whatever its side or profit, and no position is closed. Drift's docs say the same: 'paid for pro-rata (by base amount) by all open positions'. A spot residual instead lowers the deposit interest index, a pro-rata haircut to every lender in that market.

Hyperliquid and Binance use the same funding skeleton: F = average premium index + clamp(interest rate - premium index, -0.05%, +0.05%). Hyperliquid builds it from impact prices against its oracle price. Cross margin pools collateral across positions, so liquidation decisions become coupled. Isolated margin posts collateral separately for positions in different assets. Hyperliquid and Crypto.com use the same meanings: cross collateral is shared by all positions, and isolated margin is limited to one position.

Jupiter Perps documents per-position collateral and does not describe cross-margin. Shorts always use USDC collateral and a second same-asset, same-side position merges into one with sizes and collateral added. Jupiter does not prompt for more collateral before liquidation, and withdrawing collateral raises leverage and moves the liquidation price closer. The page states no maintenance margin ratio.

Solana perp venues fall into three backstop designs. Drift-lineage venues and Zeta use per-market or platform funds plus socialization: Drift and Velocity spread the residual over a market's open interest, Zeta over all depositors. Pool-as-counterparty venues (Jupiter's JLP markets and Flash) make liquidity providers absorb trader P&L, and Flash documents no insurance fund. Orderbook venues such as Jupiter's Beta markets liquidate on the book and state they have no ADL at launch. Queue-based ADL is the pattern of centralized exchanges and Hyperliquid, not of the Solana venues' docs read here.

Jupiter's technical reference lists a JupUSD custody account and oracle price account alongside SOL, ETH, BTC, USDC and USDT, so JupUSD is a configured JLP asset. The user-facing perps overview does not mention JupUSD and says short positions and Beta markets use USDC collateral. The JupUSD migration progress inside the pool was not found in any fetched source.

Cross margin lets every position in an account draw on one shared collateral pool. Isolated margin confines collateral to a single position. Hyperliquid, Velocity (formerly Drift) and Solflare Perps use these same meanings. The mode sets how far a liquidation reaches: an isolated loss stops at that position's margin, while a cross loss can consume the whole pool.

Jupiter Perps records collateral on each position, and its docs never name cross or isolated margin. A user can hold at most six JLP-market positions, one per asset and side. A second order on the same asset and side merges into the existing position and adds sizes and collaterals. Withdrawing collateral raises leverage and moves the liquidation price toward the market, and Jupiter does not prompt for more collateral before liquidating. Per-position collateral is the behavior described, not a documented label.

HIP-3 builder-deployed markets inherit Hypercore liquidation and ADL (trade.xyz docs). That page says an onchain backstop liquidator is live only for cross-margin-enabled XYZ assets and that backstop liquidation through the liquidator vault is 'only applicable for cross-margin enabled assets', which it says makes those assets significantly less likely to experience ADL; XYZ assets use an 'XYZ Relayer Mark' price. Single-source and undated; it implies HIP-3 assets without the backstop liquidator rely more on ADL.

The word isolated names several unrelated things in the Drift family. Isolated margin positions keep collateral per perp position in the program code. Isolated pools are separate spot collateral pools for swaps and leveraged borrow and lend: Velocity's page says perp orders are rejected there and no isolated pool has been deployed on the exchange yet. The Isolated contract tier gives a perp market a $0 insurance cap and extra account constraints, and the program rejects an Isolated-tier liability with IsolatedAssetTierViolation if the user has margin trading enabled. Solflare Perps launched with isolated margin only. Each position has its own collateral, so liquidation risks only that position's collateral, and cross margin was stated as not available at launch.

In cross margin, a deposit other than the quote asset counts at less than its market value. Velocity applies separate initial and maintenance asset weights below 1, and borrows carry liability weights above 1. The initial weight shrinks once a spot market's total deposits pass a scale-start threshold. An IMF factor lowers weights for large holdings: weight = min(base weight, 1.1 / (1 + sqrt(size) * imf factor)). Neodyme's audit describes the same weighting for Drift, where a requirement is met only if weighted assets are at least weighted liabilities.

In Drift's Rust the publisher-count check (has_sufficient_number_of_data_points = num_qt >= min(num, 3)) runs only for legacy push-format Pyth accounts (Pyth, Pyth1K, Pyth1M, PythStableCoin) and only in mainnet-beta builds. The pull-format (PriceUpdateV2) and Pyth Lazer paths leave the flag at true, and Switchboard On-Demand hard-codes it true. Velocity's docs say the insufficient-data-points grade applies to 'Pyth push only'.

Crypto.com's isolated perpetuals ring-fence margin for one position and allow one isolated position per symbol, either long or short. Its help article says adding margin moves the liquidation price further away, and raising leverage leaves the liquidation price unchanged. The article does not give maintenance margin rates or a liquidation formula.

Hyperliquid liquidations can be audited from public artifacts, not source code. The node is closed source, so OtterSec reverse-engineered the hl-node binary. Historical blocks are available from s3://hl-mainnet-node-data/explorer_blocks. The public L2 order-book archive supports minute-level panels (Lim), the on-chain fill log supports per-fill ADL replay (Chitra), and the info API's vaultDetails endpoint returns HLP history (CoinGecko). Chitra notes Binance's account-level ADL data are not public.

In Velocity, only tiers A, B and C draw on the shared insurance fund. A Speculative, Highly Speculative or Isolated market draws nothing, and a new market starts at Highly Speculative until an admin promotes it. Bad debt in a zero-cover market goes to the estate, the market's in-transit insurance fee, the AMM fee-provision clawback, and then to that market's own traders. An admin can re-tier a market under an open position, which changes its insurance cap at once.

The Velocity SDK mirrors three TWAP safeguards in its funding projection. (a) A mark TWAP left unwritten for more than three funding periods (and at least one hour) is discarded and re-seeded from the oracle TWAP. (b) A bid/ask-crank sample may carry at most max(funding period / 60, 60 seconds) of weight. (c) If the oracle was invalid, the oracle TWAP is pulled toward the mark TWAP in proportion to the invalid time; over trade-less intervals the mark TWAP is pulled toward the oracle TWAP. The docs describe the same behaviour: funding is damped, not skipped, while a feed is invalid.

Hyperliquid's Info API exposes funding, markPx, oraclePx and premium per asset through metaAndAssetCtxs, and fundingHistory returns one record per hour with the rate actually charged. fundingHistory does not return the oracle price, so estimating past payments needs a separate oracle or mark series.

Each spot market has its own insurance fund, held in that market's asset. The quote-asset fund backs every perp. Stakers hold shares. To unstake, a staker requests, waits (13 days by default, set per spot market), then withdraws. The payout uses the lower of the share price at request and at withdrawal. A draw after the request therefore reaches the staker and a gain does not.

Jupiter's Perps docs list three onchain price oracles: Edge by Chaos Labs as primary, with Chainlink and Pyth for verification and fallback. Chaos Labs announced Edge with Jupiter on 2024-09-12 as the replacement for Jupiter's 'legacy oracle architecture'. The docs tell integrators who read the custody account's dovesOracle field to migrate to dovesAgOracle.

Switchboard gave three reasons: AI tooling has lowered the cost of building an in-house oracle, a long bear market cut demand from new chains and protocols, and large data buyers now contract directly with data providers (the post cites Hyperliquid's data deal with S&P). Solana Compass and Crypto Briefing both relay the same Switchboard post.

Drift's docs say every asset deposited into a subaccount backs every position in that subaccount, so cross-margin scope is the subaccount. The margin calculation struct compares one cross total_collateral against one cross margin_requirement.

Velocity aims to charge longs and shorts the same rate. The AMM takes the other side of any long/short imbalance and pays from its own retained equity: at most one third of its fee pool per funding period. If the cost would exceed that, the receiving side's rate is capped, so the cumulative long and short funding rates diverge. If the AMM is the net receiver, it keeps the difference as revenue. The insurance fund is never drawn on to cover a funding shortfall.

Switchboard's stated reasons were cheaper AI-built in-house oracles, a prolonged bear market cutting demand, and large data consumers contracting directly with data providers (Hyperliquid and S&P cited as an example). Both outlets report the same Switchboard X post, so this is one origin, not two.

Switchboard let anyone create a custom data feed without gatekeeping. Protocols that relied on niche or custom feeds may not find equivalents on Pyth or RedStone. The same property matters for market listing: whoever sets a market's oracle account can point it at a feed they control.

Chitra's paper proves an ADL trilemma: no policy can satisfy exchange solvency, exchange revenue and trader fairness together. It also proves that moral hazard grows with participation, so zero-loss socialization is impossible. It argues that queue-based methods are the worst ADL policies for the top winning trade, and that capped wealth-pro-rata is the unique fair rule in its axiomatic and optimization senses. These are results of one research group on its own model. The Columbia paper studies a different objective and does not replicate them.

Misbelief: Several third-party guides state leverage or fee figures that contradict primary data. Buildix (2026-04-02, no cited source) puts Hyperliquid BTC and ETH at 50x. eco.com's Hyperliquid guide (2026-10-05) says BTC and ETH cap at 40x to 50x and calls the 0.015% tier-0 maker fee a rebate, and its Drift guide lists Jupiter at 100x and Hyperliquid at 50x. A January 2025 aggregator lists Hyperliquid at 50x. Hyperliquid's API shows BTC 40x and ETH 25x, and Jupiter's docs show 250x.

Open question: Inference, not stated by any source: because Pyth Lazer ran normally during the 2026-05-22 Pythnet outage while sponsored push feeds on Solana stopped, perp markets that read Lazer (the first source Velocity lists) would have been insulated from that outage, and markets reading push feeds would not. No source reports how any specific perp venue fared.

Controversy: Two insurance fund size figures exist and neither is verified. Drift's 18 October 2025 newsletter says about $50M against $500M+ of open interest, a 1:10 ratio. A 10 May 2026 forum post estimates roughly $20M, with $6M to $8M possibly protocol-owned, from the author's own on-chain checks. No source read gives Velocity's current fund balance.

Controversy: Hyperliquid disputes the framing of the ADL critique. Jeff Yan wrote that ADL 'does not transfer pnl to HLP', treats HLP symmetrically with users and 'has nothing to do with HLP or backstop liquidations', and that ADL net made users hundreds of millions of dollars by closing profitable shorts at favorable prices; he gave no breakdown. Dan Robinson, per the Thogiti summary and the Unchained host, argued Chitra's model was wrong because production ADL closes contracts, not equity.

Controversy: Press and critics disputed the December 2025 version. Protos reported Chitra's claim of more than $650M excess ADL, 28x the potential bad debt. Hyperliquid's Jeff Yan replied 'Those who can, do. Those who can't, fud.' and argued ADL netted users hundreds of millions by closing profitable shorts at favorable prices. A blog review by Nagu Thogiti, a later co-author of the companion paper, relayed Dan Robinson's objection that Hyperliquid ADL closes contracts, not whole equity, and said the $653M method was unpublished. Treat $653M as superseded.

Controversy: Hyperliquid's side of the ADL dispute: Jeff Yan said ADL 'does not transfer pnl to HLP', treats HLP symmetrically with users and 'has nothing to do with HLP or backstop liquidations', and that ADLs net made users hundreds of millions by closing profitable shorts at favorable prices. Dan Robinson argued the paper's model of Hyperliquid ADL was wrong because production ADL closes contracts rather than taking equity. A commentator notes Hyperliquid's ADL code is not open, so outsiders infer behavior from docs and fills.

Controversy: The $653M overshoot figure is contested. Dan Robinson argues the paper misreads Hyperliquid's ADL, which closes in contracts, not whole-equity takes. A blog review says the figure's methodology was unpublished and may reflect gross notional or equity rather than realized loss. Hyperliquid's Jeff Yan rejected the paper as FUD, and Hyperliquid supporters cited Gauntlet's investments in competitors. Protos did not independently verify any side.

Controversy: Third-party Drift leverage figures conflict with each other and with Velocity's live table. eco.com (2026-10-05) says majors reach 20x, mid-caps (JUP, JTO, PYTH, DOGE) 10x and memecoins 5x across about 35 markets. Solana Compass (2026-08-25) says SOL, BTC and ETH reach 101x and other markets 20x. Velocity's docs endpoint on 2026-11-06 shows 20x on SOL, BTC and ETH, 10x on HYPE and ZEC, and only five perp markets. A search for a 101x Drift mode found no source. Prefer the venue's own live table.

Controversy: A Buildix article dated 2026-04-02 lists Hyperliquid BTC and ETH at 50x and SOL at 40x. It cites no source and does not mention the March 2025 cut. Hyperliquid's margin-tier docs and live meta endpoint show BTC 40x, ETH 25x and SOL 20x on 2026-11-06, and no live asset on the default dex above 40x. Treat the Buildix figures as wrong for the default dex. Builder-deployed HIP-3 dexes set their own limits and are not covered by that meta response.

Controversy: Hyperliquid's current official funding page states funding is capped at 0.5% per hour, independent of asset. Several third-party guides and docs mirrors state 4% per hour, so the cap has probably changed or the mirrors are stale.

Controversy: Hyperliquid's documented funding cap is in conflict. The official funding page, fetched on 2026-11-06 and marked 'Last updated 5 days ago', says funding is capped at 0.5% per hour. trade.xyz's docs (marked 'Last updated 2 months ago') say HyperCore caps funding at 4% per hour, and Dwellir's guide (published 2026-06-11) also says 4% per hour. No changelog was found. Live API data on 2026-11-06 showed a maximum absolute hourly funding of about 0.13%, so it does not tell which cap applies.

Controversy: Hyperliquid's funding cap changed in autumn 2026. Phemex reported on 2026-09-27 that co-founder Jeff Yan said the next network upgrade would cut the cap from 4% to 0.5% per hour (the report cites PANews, not an official post). Archived copies of the official funding page still read 'capped at 4%/hour' on 2026-10-22, and the live page on 2026-11-06 reads 0.5%/hour. Guides written before the change, such as Dwellir's of 2026-06-11, still say 4%. No source states the effective date.
